tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

Both pages find their host through `window.wx.postMessage(json)` and receive host
envelopes through `window.__jusprinBridge.deliver(envelope)` (`WebShared/bridgeClient.ts`).
Copy `resources/jusprin/{agent,home}/index.html` to a scratch dir, inject
`<script>` right after `<head>` that (1) defines `window.wx` answering `hello` with
`hello_ack` + a full `state`, and (2) exposes `window.fake.deliver(type, payload)`;
serve with `python3 -m http.server` and open `agent.html?panel=printer` /
`home.html` via `preview_start`. Drive it with `javascript_tool`: deliver
`assistant_started` with no `assistant_delta` to freeze a streaming empty turn,
`printer_session` to pin a card, `printer_added` for Home's receipt strip. A file
drop works with `new DragEvent('drop', {dataTransfer})` on `.app--printer`.
Envelope: `{protocol:'jusprin-agent-bridge'|'jusprin-home-bridge', version:1, id, type, payload}`.
Used 2026-09-19 to review branch these-commits-are-probably-wrong in ~10 minutes.

**Why:** the desktop tools were locked by another session and background
`app_click` never reaches WKWebView content, so page-level states (streaming
activity line, compact photo chip, leave dialog, receipt strip) had no other cheap
proof. It proves page rendering only; host behaviour (e.g. the 256 KiB image
preview cap `kInlineImagePreviewCap` in `AgentHost.cpp`) must be replicated in
the fake by hand or checked live.

**How to apply:** reach for this before building a full app + datadir copy when the
question is "what does the page draw for state X". Pair with [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]]
for the host side. Related: [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]].
===== prove-guard-tests-fail-first

name: prove-guard-tests-fail-first
description: A lint-style test that reads a source file must be shown failing on injected drift before it counts; Vitest hands CSS imports (even ?raw) back empty in the AgentUI setup.
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 1b302f25-67a5-44d7-9f2c-02b68b2a0bb8
  modified: 2026-09-07T23:29:44.393Z
---

In `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI`, `import css from './styles.css?raw'` under Vitest resolves to an empty string, and `new URL('./x', import.meta.url)` is not a `file:` URL in the jsdom environment. A stylesheet-guard test written either way passed green while asserting nothing.

**Why:** Vitest's CSS handling short-circuits the import before Vite's `?raw` asset path runs, so every regex over the "stylesheet" matched nothing. Only appending a deliberate `border-radius: 4px` to the file and watching the suite stay green exposed it.

**How to apply:** Read source files in tests with `readFileSync(join(__dirname, ...))` and assert the text is non-empty. For any guard test that scans a file, inject the violation it exists to catch, confirm it fails naming the offender, then restore. Related: [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]], [[fork-rebase-risk-verify-before-claiming]].

How Kenneth wants a re-sync done (2026-10-13): back up first, re-import, then
compare the backup with the new import so nothing already in sync regresses.
The method that worked, in order:
- rebuild from the old reads and require byte-identical output (proves the
  scripts);
- re-read Figma with the old script and diff the reads (proves Figma unchanged:
  all 14 files were identical);
- only then change scripts, and explain every file `compare_builds.py` reports;
- score every artboard against Figma's own page screenshots
  (`visual_compare.py`) and allow no artboard to score worse.

of Figma (0–255 scale) went from 99 to 122 of 186; all 37 cards and 163 of 166
spec files came out byte-identical; tokens matched Figma's variables exactly.

had added behind dark variants (Figma has none), frames forced dark by a "dark"
in their name (use Figma's `explicitVariableModes` instead), a frame half light
and half dark through a nested mode, sets whose background is a two-stop linear
gradient, Figma's GRID layout (children need their own positions), and small
frames centred in the 40px-minimum artboard instead of top-left.

name: figma-dump-then-measure-parity
description: "Fast way to bring a JusPrin web page to Figma parity: structural Figma dump, real-component fixtures written to a review page, getBoundingClientRect compared with Figma sizes, then the shell harness capture modes for the live app."
metadata:

---

Used 2026-10-06 for the Agent UI state matrices (worktree
handoff-agent-ui-figma-parity-c8a09a); 100 states matched Figma card heights to
the pixel in one session.

1. Dump the Figma nodes as text once ([[figma-mcp-view-seat-limit]] has the
   20 KB-per-call recipe). Figma strokes are drawn inside the box, so draw card
   borders as `box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px` and give primary buttons `border: 0`;
   otherwise every card is 2 px taller than its frame.
2. Fixtures live in `AgentUI/src/visual/*.visual-cases.tsx`, rendered by
   `AgentUiStateMatrix.preview.test.tsx` (helper `src/test/visual.tsx`).
   `PREVIEW_OUT=/abs/page.html npx vitest run AgentUiStateMatrix` writes the
   page; serve it with `python3 -m http.server` and open
   `?show=<case>,<case>&mode=dark&dock=320` in the built-in browser.
3. Measure, do not eyeball: a `javascript_tool` call returning
   `getBoundingClientRect()` for each case against the dump's WxH finds 1-2 px
   errors a screenshot hides. Run JS in a separate call from `navigate` (the
   script can run on the old document).
4. Live app without mouse or screen capture: `JusPrinShellHarness` (target
   `shell_integration_harness`) `--light-ui|--dark-ui --figma-timeline-capture
   <dir>`, `--chat-restoration-capture <dir>`, plus the default, `--task-chat`
   and `--mcp` runs. Each needs a fresh scratch `HOME`, takes under a minute,
   and writes PNGs of the real WKWebView. The harness clicks page selectors
   (`.project-updates-actions button.primary`, `.chat-dialog button.primary`,
   `[data-testid="plan-live-plan"] button.primary`), so grep
   `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` before renaming a class.
5. CMake's `jusprin_web` target runs `npm ci`, which empties `node_modules`
   for a few seconds; a vitest run at that moment fails with "Cannot find
   package chai". Retry.

===== agent-panel-css-namespaces
---
name: agent-panel-css-namespaces
description: AgentUI styles.css has no CSS modules — the setup-* class prefix belongs to the agent setup screens, so new components need their own prefix
metadata:
  type: project
---

`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/styles.css` is one flat global stylesheet
with no CSS modules or scoping. The `setup-*` prefix is already taken by the
agent **setup screens** (`Setup.tsx`, `SetupLocalTool.tsx`) — `.setup-card`
there is `display: flex; flex-direction: column` on a lavender
`--surface-selected` ground.

**Why:** a new component that reuses one of those names silently inherits
`display: flex` and leaks its own rules back onto the setup screens. This cost
real time once: the "Current setup" card reused `.setup-card`, which defeated
its `white-space: nowrap` title clamp and re-tinted its background. Both
suites stayed green — jsdom does no layout, so no unit test can see it.

**How to apply:** pick a prefix that does not already appear in styles.css
(`grep -n '^\.<prefix>' src/styles.css`), and verify layout by rendering the
real component at real width rather than trusting tests. The pattern that
works: `SetupCard.preview.test.tsx` uses `renderToStaticMarkup` plus the real
styles.css and design tokens to emit a page of every state, served over a
local http server and measured in the browser (`scrollWidth > clientWidth`,
row heights). See [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]].

---

description: "The two Claude artifacts mirroring the Figma file JusPrin v2 (a Design System and a Design canvas): URLs, where the re-sync tools and backups live, how a re-sync is proven safe, what was measured on 2026-10-13, known gaps."

Two private artifacts in Kenneth's Claude account mirror the Figma file
([[figma-jusprin-v2-file]]). Since 2026-10-20 these artifacts ARE the source of truth ([[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]]); edit them directly. The Figma re-sync steps below are history.

1. Design System: https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL (version 9)
   - `tokens.json` + `tokens.css`, 37 coded React components (`window.JusPrin`).
   - Each component card: every variant Figma draws, a Light and a Dark panel,
     then the coded component. The page lists them as one flat table in bundle
     order with code names; it draws no group headings.
   - `screens/<page>/<screen>.spec.txt` (166) + `screens/index.json`: plain
     files for agents, one resolved line per layer.
2. Design canvas "JusPrin v2": https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v
   (version 7): 10 pages with Figma's names in Figma's order, 198 artboards at
   their Figma x,y and in Figma's layer order, each drawn in the Light or Dark
   mode Figma sets on it; "… · Light & Dark" review frames are drawn whole.

Tools, reads and backups are durable now, outside the repo:
`~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/figma-mirror/` — start with
its `README.md` (step-by-step re-sync). `published/` is an exact copy of what is
live; `backup-2026-10-13-before-reimport/` holds the earlier state with the
scripts that reproduce it byte for byte.

How Kenneth wants a re-sync done (2026-10-13): back up first, re-import, then
compare the backup with the new import so nothing already in sync regresses.
The method that worked, in order:
- rebuild from the old reads and require byte-identical output (proves the
  scripts);
- re-read Figma with the old script and diff the reads (proves Figma unchanged:
  all 14 files were identical);
- only then change scripts, and explain every file `compare_builds.py` reports;
- score every artboard against Figma's own page screenshots
  (`visual_compare.py`) and allow no artboard to score worse.
Result of that run: 0 artboards further from Figma, 36 closer; boards within 5
of Figma (0–255 scale) went from 99 to 122 of 186; all 37 cards and 163 of 166
spec files came out byte-identical; tokens matched Figma's variables exactly.

What the screenshot comparison caught that file checks could not: dark panels I
had added behind dark variants (Figma has none), frames forced dark by a "dark"
in their name (use Figma's `explicitVariableModes` instead), a frame half light
and half dark through a nested mode, sets whose background is a two-stop linear
gradient, Figma's GRID layout (children need their own positions), and small
frames centred in the 40px-minimum artboard instead of top-left.

Other traps: an absolutely positioned layer followed by in-flow siblings paints
over them in HTML (give the later siblings `position:relative`); Figma tints
icons with a mask plus a coloured rectangle; the Artifact tool's bulk read
prints small text files into context, so have a background agent do large
backups; a session scratchpad is wiped on restart — never keep the only copy of
tools there; when two reads of a page exist, keep the later one by timestamp.

Known gaps: photographs and 3D renders are flat placeholders (the 16 worst
scores are all such screens); radial and image fills are placeholders; Figma
stacks 12 dark screens on top of light ones on "Printer & Material Settings"
and the canvas keeps that; ProjectCard and PrinterCard variants are stacked in
Figma and laid out in a row on the canvas; "Add Printer Flow (Obsolete)" is not
read; Notice/Strip drifts a few px vertically.

Figma vs code differences Kenneth has not ruled on (the artifacts hold Figma's):
dark status colours (Figma #4CAF82 / #E07080 / #E8B84A, code #58B894 / #F07A8E /
#E9B960), `radius/full` 10 vs `pill` 9999, Button/Icon 32px vs 26px, Menu/Row
36px full-width hover vs the app's 32px inset rows
([[header-menu-values-kenneth-kept]]). See also [[figma-mcp-view-seat-limit]]
and [[claude-in-chrome-lives-in-claude-profile]].

Direct editing (2026-10-20): work on a copy of the live files (`figma-mirror/live-<date>` -> `work/`),
publish only the changed files, then rsync `work/` into `published/`. The canvas holds its own copy of the
design system in `project/ds/jusprin/` (tokens.css/json, components/bundle.*) — change both artifacts
together. `tools/composer/render.py` screenshots boards with headless Chrome (no type runtime needed);
measure natural board heights in the built-in browser and fix both the board file and canvas.json
(`resize_board.py`). `index.d.ts` must be published with contentType text/plain. The DS card height lives
in the `@dsCard height=` comment. Added then: `surface-raised-hover` (menu-row highlight, dark #3B3047) and
`component-composer-maxLines` (8); the new Composer is drawn by `tools/composer/composer_html.py`.
===== figma-dump-then-measure-parity
---
name: figma-dump-then-measure-parity
description: "Fast way to bring a JusPrin web page to Figma parity: structural Figma dump, real-component fixtures written to a review page, getBoundingClientRect compared with Figma sizes, then the shell harness capture modes for the live app."
metadata:
  type: reference
---

Used 2026-10-06 for the Agent UI state matrices (worktree
handoff-agent-ui-figma-parity-c8a09a); 100 states matched Figma card heights to
the pixel in one session.

1. Dump the Figma nodes as text once ([[figma-mcp-view-seat-limit]] has the
   20 KB-per-call recipe). Figma strokes are drawn inside the box, so draw card
   borders as `box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px` and give primary buttons `border: 0`;
   otherwise every card is 2 px taller than its frame.
2. Fixtures live in `AgentUI/src/visual/*.visual-cases.tsx`, rendered by
   `AgentUiStateMatrix.preview.test.tsx` (helper `src/test/visual.tsx`).
   `PREVIEW_OUT=/abs/page.html npx vitest run AgentUiStateMatrix` writes the
   page; serve it with `python3 -m http.server` and open
   `?show=<case>,<case>&mode=dark&dock=320` in the built-in browser.
3. Measure, do not eyeball: a `javascript_tool` call returning
   `getBoundingClientRect()` for each case against the dump's WxH finds 1-2 px
   errors a screenshot hides. Run JS in a separate call from `navigate` (the
   script can run on the old document).
4. Live app without mouse or screen capture: `JusPrinShellHarness` (target
   `shell_integration_harness`) `--light-ui|--dark-ui --figma-timeline-capture
   <dir>`, `--chat-restoration-capture <dir>`, plus the default, `--task-chat`
   and `--mcp` runs. Each needs a fresh scratch `HOME`, takes under a minute,
   and writes PNGs of the real WKWebView. The harness clicks page selectors
   (`.project-updates-actions button.primary`, `.chat-dialog button.primary`,
   `[data-testid="plan-live-plan"] button.primary`), so grep
   `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` before renaming a class.
5. CMake's `jusprin_web` target runs `npm ci`, which empties `node_modules`
   for a few seconds; a vitest run at that moment fails with "Cannot find
   package chai". Retry.

**2026-10-06 addendum (onboarding takeover, Codex worktree ea9a):** exported
reference images handed over by another agent can be stale: the welcome frame had
lost a row since its export. Get current renders from Figma itself: a read-only
`use_figma` script calling `await node.screenshot({ scale: 1 })` per frame returns
at most 5 images per call, each saved as a PNG under the session's
`tool-results/` folder (8 frames = 2 calls). With the dump, the Home onboarding
page matched six of seven frame rectangles on the first build. To show Home page
states in the real app without clicking (background `app_click` never reaches
the web view, and full-screen approval times out when Kenneth is away): seed
`jusprin_onboarding` in a scratch datadir's `JusPrin2.conf`, relaunch, resize the
window to 1280x832 with System Events, and `app_screenshot` the main window id.
===== agent-panel-css-namespaces
---
name: agent-panel-css-namespaces
description: AgentUI styles.css has no CSS modules — the setup-* class prefix belongs to the agent setup screens, so new components need their own prefix
metadata:
  type: project
---

`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/styles.css` is one flat global stylesheet
with no CSS modules or scoping. The `setup-*` prefix is already taken by the
agent **setup screens** (`Setup.tsx`, `SetupLocalTool.tsx`) — `.setup-card`
there is `display: flex; flex-direction: column` on a lavender
`--surface-selected` ground.

**Why:** a new component that reuses one of those names silently inherits
`display: flex` and leaks its own rules back onto the setup screens. This cost
real time once: the "Current setup" card reused `.setup-card`, which defeated
its `white-space: nowrap` title clamp and re-tinted its background. Both
suites stayed green — jsdom does no layout, so no unit test can see it.

**How to apply:** pick a prefix that does not already appear in styles.css
(`grep -n '^\.<prefix>' src/styles.css`), and verify layout by rendering the
real component at real width rather than trusting tests. The pattern that
works: `SetupCard.preview.test.tsx` uses `renderToStaticMarkup` plus the real
styles.css and design tokens to emit a page of every state, served over a
local http server and measured in the browser (`scrollWidth > clientWidth`,
row heights). See [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]].

19	  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
20	```

22	CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

331	spec files came out byte-identical; tokens matched Figma's variables exactly.
332	
333	What the screenshot comparison caught that file checks could not: dark panels I
334	had added behind dark variants (Figma has none), frames forced dark by a "dark"
335	in their name (use Figma's `explicitVariableModes` instead), a frame half light
336	and half dark through a nested mode, sets whose background is a two-stop linear
337	gradient, Figma's GRID layout (children need their own positions), and small
338	frames centred in the 40px-minimum artboard instead of top-left.
339	
340	Other traps: an absolutely positioned layer followed by in-flow siblings paints
341	over them in HTML (give the later siblings `position:relative`); Figma tints
342	icons with a mask plus a coloured rectangle; the Artifact tool's bulk read
343	prints small text files into context, so have a background agent do large
344	backups; a session scratchpad is wiped on restart — never keep the only copy of
345	tools there; when two reads of a page exist, keep the later one by timestamp.
346	
347	Known gaps: photographs and 3D renders are flat placeholders (the 16 worst
348	scores are all such screens); radial and image fills are placeholders; Figma
349	stacks 12 dark screens on top of light ones on "Printer & Material Settings"
350	and the canvas keeps that; ProjectCard and PrinterCard variants are stacked in
351	Figma and laid out in a row on the canvas; "Add Printer Flow (Obsolete)" is not
352	read; Notice/Strip drifts a few px vertically.
353	
354	Figma vs code differences Kenneth has not ruled on (the artifacts hold Figma's):
355	dark status colours (Figma #4CAF82 / #E07080 / #E8B84A, code #58B894 / #F07A8E /
356	#E9B960), `radius/full` 10 vs `pill` 9999, Button/Icon 32px vs 26px, Menu/Row
357	36px full-width hover vs the app's 32px inset rows
358	([[header-menu-values-kenneth-kept]]). See also [[figma-mcp-view-seat-limit]]
359	and [[claude-in-chrome-lives-in-claude-profile]].
360	
361	Direct editing (2026-10-20): work on a copy of the live files (`figma-mirror/live-<date>` -> `work/`),
362	publish only the changed files, then rsync `work/` into `published/`. The canvas holds its own copy of the
363	design system in `project/ds/jusprin/` (tokens.css/json, components/bundle.*) — change both artifacts
364	together. `tools/composer/render.py` screenshots boards with headless Chrome (no type runtime needed);
365	measure natural board heights in the built-in browser and fix both the board file and canvas.json
366	(`resize_board.py`). `index.d.ts` must be published with contentType text/plain. The DS card height lives
367	in the `@dsCard height=` comment. Added then: `surface-raised-hover` (menu-row highlight, dark #3B3047) and
368	`component-composer-maxLines` (8); the new Composer is drawn by `tools/composer/composer_html.py`.
369	===== figma-dump-then-measure-parity
370	---
371	name: figma-dump-then-measure-parity
372	description: "Fast way to bring a JusPrin web page to Figma parity: structural Figma dump, real-component fixtures written to a review page, getBoundingClientRect compared with Figma sizes, then the shell harness capture modes for the live app."
373	metadata:
374	  type: reference
375	---
376	
377	Used 2026-10-06 for the Agent UI state matrices (worktree
378	handoff-agent-ui-figma-parity-c8a09a); 100 states matched Figma card heights to
379	the pixel in one session.
380	
381	1. Dump the Figma nodes as text once ([[figma-mcp-view-seat-limit]] has the
382	   20 KB-per-call recipe). Figma strokes are drawn inside the box, so draw card
383	   borders as `box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px` and give primary buttons `border: 0`;
384	   otherwise every card is 2 px taller than its frame.
385	2. Fixtures live in `AgentUI/src/visual/*.visual-cases.tsx`, rendered by
386	   `AgentUiStateMatrix.preview.test.tsx` (helper `src/test/visual.tsx`).
387	   `PREVIEW_OUT=/abs/page.html npx vitest run AgentUiStateMatrix` writes the
388	   page; serve it with `python3 -m http.server` and open
389	   `?show=<case>,<case>&mode=dark&dock=320` in the built-in browser.
390	3. Measure, do not eyeball: a `javascript_tool` call returning
391	   `getBoundingClientRect()` for each case against the dump's WxH finds 1-2 px
392	   errors a screenshot hides. Run JS in a separate call from `navigate` (the
393	   script can run on the old document).
394	4. Live app without mouse or screen capture: `JusPrinShellHarness` (target
395	   `shell_integration_harness`) `--light-ui|--dark-ui --figma-timeline-capture
396	   <dir>`, `--chat-restoration-capture <dir>`, plus the default, `--task-chat`
397	   and `--mcp` runs. Each needs a fresh scratch `HOME`, takes under a minute,
398	   and writes PNGs of the real WKWebView. The harness clicks page selectors
399	   (`.project-updates-actions button.primary`, `.chat-dialog button.primary`,
400	   `[data-testid="plan-live-plan"] button.primary`), so grep
401	   `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` before renaming a class.
402	5. CMake's `jusprin_web` target runs `npm ci`, which empties `node_modules`
403	   for a few seconds; a vitest run at that moment fails with "Cannot find
404	   package chai". Retry.
405	
406	**2026-10-06 addendum (onboarding takeover, Codex worktree ea9a):** exported
407	reference images handed over by another agent can be stale: the welcome frame had
408	lost a row since its export. Get current renders from Figma itself: a read-only
409	`use_figma` script calling `await node.screenshot({ scale: 1 })` per frame returns
410	at most 5 images per call, each saved as a PNG under the session's
411	`tool-results/` folder (8 frames = 2 calls). With the dump, the Home onboarding
412	page matched six of seven frame rectangles on the first build. To show Home page
413	states in the real app without clicking (background `app_click` never reaches
414	the web view, and full-screen approval times out when Kenneth is away): seed
415	`jusprin_onboarding` in a scratch datadir's `JusPrin2.conf`, relaunch, resize the
416	window to 1280x832 with System Events, and `app_screenshot` the main window id.
417	===== agent-panel-css-namespaces
418	---
419	name: agent-panel-css-namespaces
420	description: AgentUI styles.css has no CSS modules — the setup-* class prefix belongs to the agent setup screens, so new components need their own prefix
421	metadata:
422	  type: project
423	---
424	
425	`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/styles.css` is one flat global stylesheet
426	with no CSS modules or scoping. The `setup-*` prefix is already taken by the
427	agent **setup screens** (`Setup.tsx`, `SetupLocalTool.tsx`) — `.setup-card`
428	there is `display: flex; flex-direction: column` on a lavender
429	`--surface-selected` ground.
430	
431	**Why:** a new component that reuses one of those names silently inherits
432	`display: flex` and leaks its own rules back onto the setup screens. This cost
433	real time once: the "Current setup" card reused `.setup-card`, which defeated
434	its `white-space: nowrap` title clamp and re-tinted its background. Both
435	suites stayed green — jsdom does no layout, so no unit test can see it.
436	
437	**How to apply:** pick a prefix that does not already appear in styles.css
438	(`grep -n '^\.<prefix>' src/styles.css`), and verify layout by rendering the
439	real component at real width rather than trusting tests. The pattern that
440	works: `SetupCard.preview.test.tsx` uses `renderToStaticMarkup` plus the real
441	styles.css and design tokens to emit a page of every state, served over a
442	local http server and measured in the browser (`scrollWidth > clientWidth`,
443	row heights). See [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]].
444	===== header-menu-values-kenneth-kept
445	---
446	name: header-menu-values-kenneth-kept
447	description: "The header chip and popover menu dimensions Kenneth reverted to on 2026-09-07; a later commit message described the rejected look, and a token contract copied it by mistake"
448	metadata: 
449	  node_type: memory
450	  type: project
451	  originSessionId: 598f26fe-b466-4336-928e-14d10d45e1f7
452	  modified: 2026-09-08T16:34:06.633Z
453	---
454	
455	**Superseded 2026-10-20:** Kenneth chose Figma's sizes after seeing both side by side; see [[design-token-sync-decisions]]. Kept as history.
456	
457	Commit "Revert my header menu restyling: it looked worse and I could not
458	explain why" (2026-09-07, on jusprin-newui) is the authority for the header:
459	chip halves 26 tall, standard radius 4, menu rows 32 tall (44 with a second
460	line) with radius 4 and a 4 DIP side inset, popover padding 4 top and bottom
461	with no gap between rows, popup border Deflate(1) at radius 8.
462	
463	The earlier commit "Follow the design-system components, and settle the
464	standard radius at 6" describes the opposite values (28, 36, no radius, full
465	width, padding 8, gap 2) as measured from Figma. Those were tried and
466	rejected. On 2026-09-08 a token contract copied them from that message and a
467	migration re-applied the rejected look before it was caught.
468	
469	**How to apply:** when writing tokens or docs for the header, read the code
470	on jusprin-newui, not commit messages or Figma. Figma's chip component still
471	says radius 6 and the Figma "Radius" variables are unbound; the code is
472	ahead of the design file here. See [[figma-jusprin-v2-file]].
473	===== ask-decisions-in-full
474	---
475	name: ask-decisions-in-full
476	description: When a decision is Kenneth's, state it with complete information (what, why it is his, the options, the consequence of each, my recommendation); never a shorthand like "the go to catch the main checkout up" or "the three harness decisions". Asked 2026-10-14 after two such shorthands.
477	metadata:
478	  type: feedback
479	---
480	
481	On 2026-10-14 I ended a reply with "two things are waiting on you: the go to catch the main checkout up with the rewritten branch, and the three harness decisions from the critique report." Kenneth could not tell whether the first was a decision he had to make, and said the second left him guessing what the decisions were. He asked that this be recorded as a standing rule.
482	
483	**Why:** a phrase that only makes sense with my working context reads as jargon to him, and a decision he cannot understand is a decision he cannot make. He had no earlier rule about this in CLAUDE.md or memory; the nearest is [[write-like-a-person]].
484	
485	**How to apply:** every time I need Kenneth to decide something, write it out in full, in its own paragraph or bullet: what the decision is, why it is his and not mine, the options with what each one does and costs, and which one I recommend. Never refer to a decision by a label, a count, or a report it lives in. Check the last paragraph of every reply for this before sending. Related: [[write-like-a-person]], [[report-outcomes-not-obstacles]].
486	
487	**Added 2026-10-18:** a decision for Kenneth is phrased as a question that ends with "?". He pointed out that three of four "decisions" I listed were statements ("The bed-temperature warning. Tell the model about it, or keep matching..."), and only the one that read as a question was answerable. Each item: the question with "?", the options with consequences, then my recommendation.
488	
489	**Added 2026-10-19:** a third repeat. I ended a status report with five one-line "still open" items ("Output limit. The Anthropic profile sets 16,000 tokens... One number in the profile."). Kenneth: "I can understand none of these questions since you did not provide the information and the contacts I needed to answer them." A short status recap is not the place for decisions; each needs its own paragraph with the mechanism explained (what the number does, what happens at the limit, what it costs), not just the knob's name. Also check whether an item is a decision at all: one of the five (minProperties in strict mode) had no user-facing effect and should not have been listed.
490	===== write-like-a-person
491	---
492	name: write-like-a-person
493	description: Kenneth finds clipped, label-style bullets ("One home per kind of thing. Standing policy in X, facts in Y.") strange and asked twice on 2026-10-14 to "talk like a human"; write full plain sentences as to a colleague.
494	metadata:
495	  type: feedback
496	---
497	
498	On 2026-10-14 Kenneth replied to two bullets in a prompt critique ("Mechanics live in the harness, not the prompt. Read-only tools on an explain turn, argument validation, …" and "One home per kind of thing. Standing policy in instructions, facts in a tagged context block, …") with "I don't know why you talk this way. Really strange. Can you talk like a human?"
499	
500	**Why:** compressed noun-phrase bullets and slogans read as jargon; he wants to be told things the way a colleague would say them out loud, with the concrete case first and the general point after.
501	
502	**How to apply:** write full sentences with a subject and a verb. Say the concrete thing ("the app currently pastes the project JSON into your message right after what you typed") before any principle. No label-colon fragments, no aphorisms, no abstract nouns standing in for an explanation. When a point needs a technical term, say what it means in the same sentence. Related: [[report-outcomes-not-obstacles]], [[investigation-report-four-part-frame]].

===== jusprin-worktree-build
---
name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).
===== web-bundles-committed-artifact-state
---
name: web-bundles-committed-artifact-state
description: "SHIPPED 2026-09-14: Agent/Home React bundles are now CMake-built and gitignored, with JUSPRIN_AGENT_DEV_URL/JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL for Vite HMR. Superseded the prior committed-artifact model."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: c6ef8ee9-0673-49c6-9bb3-69a61f005ed5
  modified: 2026-09-16T23:33:21.710Z

**This memory's own proposal shipped the same day it was written.** Commit
`5fc0efe2` on `jusprin-newui` (cherry-picked as `bef82ed2` on
`cursor/cd073db7`), "Stop committing the Agent and Home HTML; rebuild them
from TypeScript.", landed 2026-09-14 14:08 PDT — implementing exactly what
the section below used to call "proposed... pending Kenneth's decision."
Do not describe the two bundles as hand-committed or irreproducible without
re-checking; that is no longer true.

**Current state:** `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` and
`resources/jusprin/home/index.html` are CMake-built (`npm ci` + `npm run
build` when inputs change, target `jusprin_web`) and gitignored via
`resources/jusprin/.gitignore`. `AGENTS.md` notes "Node/npm is required to
build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF`
and supply the bundles." Each web view reads a dev-URL env var exactly once
at construction, no settings UI: `JUSPRIN_AGENT_DEV_URL` (default port 5173)
in `AgentWebView.cpp`, `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` (default port 5174) in
`HomeWebView.cpp`. The HMR recipe (`npm run dev` in `AgentUI/` or `HomeUI/`,
then launch the built app with the env var set) is documented in each page's
own README — `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/README.md` and
`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/HomeUI/README.md` — NOT under `agent-docs/`, which
has no HMR doc at all. The AgentUI README's old "does not require Node"
sentence was also updated in this same commit.

**Miss this caused once already:** asked whether `agent-docs` documents HMR,
a grep scoped to that directory correctly came back empty, but the answer
then over-generalized to "no HMR workflow is documented anywhere" — without
checking the component READMEs, and while citing this memory's stale
"proposal, not yet accepted" framing instead of re-verifying against the
live repo. Directory-scoped questions need directory-scoped answers, not
repo-wide conclusions; and a memory with a future decision pending is a
reason to check current state, not a substitute for it.

**Not verified:** whether [[agent-bridge-phase-2]]'s "npm bundle rebuild
rule" was updated/marked obsolete as this memory once suggested — check that
file directly before relying on it.
===== agent-bridge-phase-2
---
name: agent-bridge-phase-2
description: "Phase 2 Agent WebView bridge — where the pieces live, how to rebuild the page bundle, and the deliberate gaps."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 7bfab8f9-38be-4eae-93ac-29c4976b9118
  modified: 2026-08-31T04:48:45.227Z
---

Phase 2 (read-only deterministic Agent) implemented on `jusprin-newui` on 2026-08-30.

- Native bridge: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/` — `AgentHost` (GUI-free coordinator, owns the authoritative conversation; streaming advances only via `pump_stream()`), `DeterministicMockAgent` (`/fail`, `/flaky`, `/slow` scenarios), `AgentWebView` (wx transport + internal-error surface).
- React page: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/` (npm package). `npm run build` writes the committed single-file bundle `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html`; the C++ build never needs Node. Rebuild + recommit the bundle whenever AgentUI changes.
- Shared protocol source: `resources/jusprin/agent/protocol.json` — both `tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp` and the vitest suite assert their constants against it. Bump the version there and in `AgentProtocol.hpp`/`protocol.ts` together.
- Workspace contract gained `WorkspaceSetup` (project/printer/filament) and per-plate `sliced`; adding fields to `WorkspacePlate` breaks brace-initializers in `tests/workspace/test_workspace_contract.cpp`.
- Agent availability toggle: app config `jusprin_agent` = "0" → clean unavailable state (distinct from bridge errors by design).
- Deliberate gaps: preset changes only refresh Agent context at the next workspace event (needs a preset-changed seam, noted since Phase 1); Windows/Linux WebView untested.
- Evidence record: was `agent-docs/jusprin/agent-webview-phase-2.md`; removed 2026-08-30 at Kenny's request — recover it from git history or the Phase 2 commit message. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[jusprin-v2-poc-rebase-not-merge]].
===== fake-host-page-fixture
---
name: fake-host-page-fixture
description: "Render the built AgentUI/HomeUI bundles in the built-in browser with a scripted fake native host, to see page states the live app makes hard to catch"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 9bb21a20-a19f-4500-adcf-139798a1201d
  modified: 2026-09-19T16:55:23.039Z
---

Both pages find their host through `window.wx.postMessage(json)` and receive host
envelopes through `window.__jusprinBridge.deliver(envelope)` (`WebShared/bridgeClient.ts`).
Copy `resources/jusprin/{agent,home}/index.html` to a scratch dir, inject
`<script>` right after `<head>` that (1) defines `window.wx` answering `hello` with
`hello_ack` + a full `state`, and (2) exposes `window.fake.deliver(type, payload)`;
serve with `python3 -m http.server` and open `agent.html?panel=printer` /
`home.html` via `preview_start`. Drive it with `javascript_tool`: deliver
`assistant_started` with no `assistant_delta` to freeze a streaming empty turn,
`printer_session` to pin a card, `printer_added` for Home's receipt strip. A file
drop works with `new DragEvent('drop', {dataTransfer})` on `.app--printer`.
Envelope: `{protocol:'jusprin-agent-bridge'|'jusprin-home-bridge', version:1, id, type, payload}`.
Used 2026-09-19 to review branch these-commits-are-probably-wrong in ~10 minutes.

**Why:** the desktop tools were locked by another session and background
`app_click` never reaches WKWebView content, so page-level states (streaming
activity line, compact photo chip, leave dialog, receipt strip) had no other cheap
proof. It proves page rendering only; host behaviour (e.g. the 256 KiB image
preview cap `kInlineImagePreviewCap` in `AgentHost.cpp`) must be replicated in
the fake by hand or checked live.

**How to apply:** reach for this before building a full app + datadir copy when the
question is "what does the page draw for state X". Pair with [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]]
for the host side. Related: [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]].
===== prove-guard-tests-fail-first
---
name: prove-guard-tests-fail-first
description: A lint-style test that reads a source file must be shown failing on injected drift before it counts; Vitest hands CSS imports (even ?raw) back empty in the AgentUI setup.
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 1b302f25-67a5-44d7-9f2c-02b68b2a0bb8
  modified: 2026-09-07T23:29:44.393Z
---

In `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI`, `import css from './styles.css?raw'` under Vitest resolves to an empty string, and `new URL('./x', import.meta.url)` is not a `file:` URL in the jsdom environment. A stylesheet-guard test written either way passed green while asserting nothing.

**Why:** Vitest's CSS handling short-circuits the import before Vite's `?raw` asset path runs, so every regex over the "stylesheet" matched nothing. Only appending a deliberate `border-radius: 4px` to the file and watching the suite stay green exposed it.

**How to apply:** Read source files in tests with `readFileSync(join(__dirname, ...))` and assert the text is non-empty. For any guard test that scans a file, inject the violation it exists to catch, confirm it fails naming the offender, then restore. Related: [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]], [[fork-rebase-risk-verify-before-claiming]].
===== restore-temp-edits-from-a-copy
---
name: restore-temp-edits-from-a-copy
description: "After a temporary edit to prove a test fails, restore from a saved copy, never `git checkout <file>` — it also wipes your uncommitted work in that file."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 79e5592f-78a2-4530-83b6-126f25ab0a8d
  modified: 2026-10-18T00:23:11.256Z
---

`~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/figma-mirror/` — start with

scripts that reproduce it byte for byte.

How Kenneth wants a re-sync done (2026-10-13): back up first, re-import, then
compare the backup with the new import so nothing already in sync regresses.
The method that worked, in order:
- rebuild from the old reads and require byte-identical output (proves the
  scripts);
- re-read Figma with the old script and diff the reads (proves Figma unchanged:
  all 14 files were identical);
- only then change scripts, and explain every file `compare_builds.py` reports;
- score every artboard against Figma's own page screenshots
  (`visual_compare.py`) and allow no artboard to score worse.
Result of that run: 0 artboards further from Figma, 36 closer; boards within 5
of Figma (0–255 scale) went from 99 to 122 of 186; all 37 cards and 163 of 166
spec files came out byte-identical; tokens matched Figma's variables exactly.

had added behind dark variants (Figma has none), frames forced dark by a "dark"
in their name (use Figma's `explicitVariableModes` instead), a frame half light

===== figma-dump-then-measure-parity
---
name: figma-dump-then-measure-parity
description: "Fast way to bring a JusPrin web page to Figma parity: structural Figma dump, real-component fixtures written to a review page, getBoundingClientRect compared with Figma sizes, then the shell harness capture modes for the live app."
metadata:
  type: reference
---

Used 2026-10-06 for the Agent UI state matrices (worktree
handoff-agent-ui-figma-parity-c8a09a); 100 states matched Figma card heights to
the pixel in one session.

1. Dump the Figma nodes as text once ([[figma-mcp-view-seat-limit]] has the
   20 KB-per-call recipe). Figma strokes are drawn inside the box, so draw card
   borders as `box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px` and give primary buttons `border: 0`;
   otherwise every card is 2 px taller than its frame.
2. Fixtures live in `AgentUI/src/visual/*.visual-cases.tsx`, rendered by
   `AgentUiStateMatrix.preview.test.tsx` (helper `src/test/visual.tsx`).
   `PREVIEW_OUT=/abs/page.html npx vitest run AgentUiStateMatrix` writes the
   page; serve it with `python3 -m http.server` and open
   `?show=<case>,<case>&mode=dark&dock=320` in the built-in browser.
3. Measure, do not eyeball: a `javascript_tool` call returning
   `getBoundingClientRect()` for each case against the dump's WxH finds 1-2 px
   errors a screenshot hides. Run JS in a separate call from `navigate` (the
   script can run on the old document).
4. Live app without mouse or screen capture: `JusPrinShellHarness` (target
   `shell_integration_harness`) `--light-ui|--dark-ui --figma-timeline-capture
   <dir>`, `--chat-restoration-capture <dir>`, plus the default, `--task-chat`
   and `--mcp` runs. Each needs a fresh scratch `HOME`, takes under a minute,
   and writes PNGs of the real WKWebView. The harness clicks page selectors
   (`.project-updates-actions button.primary`, `.chat-dialog button.primary`,
   `[data-testid="plan-live-plan"] button.primary`), so grep
   `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` before renaming a class.
5. CMake's `jusprin_web` target runs `npm ci`, which empties `node_modules`
   for a few seconds; a vitest run at that moment fails with "Cannot find
   package chai". Retry.

**2026-10-06 addendum (onboarding takeover, Codex worktree ea9a):** exported
reference images handed over by another agent can be stale: the welcome frame had
lost a row since its export. Get current renders from Figma itself: a read-only
`use_figma` script calling `await node.screenshot({ scale: 1 })` per frame returns
at most 5 images per call, each saved as a PNG under the session's
`tool-results/` folder (8 frames = 2 calls). With the dump, the Home onboarding
page matched six of seven frame rectangles on the first build. To show Home page
states in the real app without clicking (background `app_click` never reaches
the web view, and full-screen approval times out when Kenneth is away): seed
`jusprin_onboarding` in a scratch datadir's `JusPrin2.conf`, relaunch, resize the
window to 1280x832 with System Events, and `app_screenshot` the main window id.

---
name: agent-panel-css-namespaces
description: AgentUI styles.css has no CSS modules — the setup-* class prefix belongs to the agent setup screens, so new components need their own prefix
metadata:

---

`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/styles.css` is one flat global stylesheet
with no CSS modules or scoping. The `setup-*` prefix is already taken by the
agent **setup screens** (`Setup.tsx`, `SetupLocalTool.tsx`) — `.setup-card`
there is `display: flex; flex-direction: column` on a lavender
`--surface-selected` ground.

**Why:** a new component that reuses one of those names silently inherits
`display: flex` and leaks its own rules back onto the setup screens. This cost
real time once: the "Current setup" card reused `.setup-card`, which defeated
its `white-space: nowrap` title clamp and re-tinted its background. Both
suites stayed green — jsdom does no layout, so no unit test can see it.

**How to apply:** pick a prefix that does not already appear in styles.css
(`grep -n '^\.<prefix>' src/styles.css`), and verify layout by rendering the
real component at real width rather than trusting tests. The pattern that
works: `SetupCard.preview.test.tsx` uses `renderToStaticMarkup` plus the real
styles.css and design tokens to emit a page of every state, served over a
local http server and measured in the browser (`scrollWidth > clientWidth`,
row heights). See [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]].

On 2026-10-14 I ended a reply with "two things are waiting on you: the go to catch the main checkout up with the rewritten branch, and the three harness decisions from the critique report." Kenneth could not tell whether the first was a decision he had to make, and said the second left him guessing what the decisions were. He asked that this be recorded as a standing rule.

**Why:** a phrase that only makes sense with my working context reads as jargon to him, and a decision he cannot understand is a decision he cannot make. He had no earlier rule about this in CLAUDE.md or memory; the nearest is [[write-like-a-person]].

**How to apply:** every time I need Kenneth to decide something, write it out in full, in its own paragraph or bullet: what the decision is, why it is his and not mine, the options with what each one does and costs, and which one I recommend. Never refer to a decision by a label, a count, or a report it lives in. Check the last paragraph of every reply for this before sending. **Added 2026-10-18:** a decision for Kenneth is phrased as a question that ends with "?". He pointed out that three of four "decisions" I listed were statements ("The bed-temperature warning. Tell the model about it, or keep matching..."), and only the one that read as a question was answerable. Each item: the question with "?", the options with consequences, then my recommendation.

**Added 2026-10-19:** a third repeat. I ended a status report with five one-line "still open" items ("Output limit. The Anthropic profile sets 16,000 tokens... One number in the profile."). Kenneth: "I can understand none of these questions since you did not provide the information and the contacts I needed to answer them." A short status recap is not the place for decisions; each needs its own paragraph with the mechanism explained (what the number does, what happens at the limit, what it costs), not just the knob's name. ===== write-like-a-person
---
name: write-like-a-person
description: Kenneth finds clipped, label-style bullets ("One home per kind of thing. Standing policy in X, facts in Y.") strange and asked twice on 2026-10-14 to "talk like a human"; write full plain sentences as to a colleague.
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-10-14 Kenneth replied to two bullets in a prompt critique ("Mechanics live in the harness, not the prompt. Read-only tools on an explain turn, argument validation, …" and "One home per kind of thing. Standing policy in instructions, facts in a tagged context block, …") with "I don't know why you talk this way. Really strange. Can you talk like a human?"

**Why:** compressed noun-phrase bullets and slogans read as jargon; he wants to be told things the way a colleague would say them out loud, with the concrete case first and the general point after.

**How to apply:** write full sentences with a subject and a verb. Say the concrete thing ("the app currently pastes the project JSON into your message right after what you typed") before any principle. No label-colon fragments, no aphorisms, no abstract nouns standing in for an explanation. When a point needs a technical term, say what it means in the same sentence. Related: [[report-outcomes-not-obstacles]], [[investigation-report-four-part-frame]].

# JusPrin production documentation

This directory is the canonical starting point for production work on `jusprin-newui`. It preserves the durable product and engineering decisions from `jusprin-v2-poc` without importing the POC's temporary windows, probes, static mocks, generated evidence, or environment-gated startup paths.

Read these documents in order:

1. [Product definition](product-definition.md) — the human/agent boundary, required product surfaces, workflow, and visibility rules.
2. [Production architecture](architecture.md) — the selected native/WebView architecture, ownership rules, component boundaries, and implementation sequence.
3. [Engineering and verification method](engineering-method.md) — how to assess risk and what evidence is required before calling a feature complete.
4. [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md) — known Orca behaviors, lifecycle traps, event and history constraints, and testing lessons.
5. [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md) — required before changing any OrcaSlicer-owned file: where a seam belongs, why additive beats rewritten, how to leave a conflict that resolves correctly, and what evidence a change must record.
6. [Design system](design-system.md) — brand behavior, semantic UI tokens, typography, spacing, accessibility, and asset rules.
7. [POC reference](poc-reference.md) — exact pointers to the spike-only documents, code, commits, logs, screenshots, and generated brand artifacts left on `jusprin-v2-poc`.
8. [Tool extension guide](mcp-tool-extension-guide.md) — shared Agent/MCP contracts, process-settings workflow, execution and verification requirements.
9. [Local autosave and version history](autosave-version-history.md) — managed project storage, migration, restore, export, retention, and failure behavior.

Printer UI without hardware (Bambu in-process fake; control file; isolated app): [Fake Bambu README](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md). Print-host (Klipper/Moonraker) simulation stays on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter`.

## Governing decisions

- JusPrin is an AI-piloted 3D-printing product built on OrcaSlicer, not a replacement slicing engine.
- OrcaSlicer's C++ model, slicing pipeline, viewport, geometry operations, project serialization, and undo stack remain authoritative.
- The production application stays native C++/wxWidgets/OpenGL. The Agent conversation uses a local React/TypeScript application inside `wxWebView`.
- JavaScript renders state and submits typed commands; it never owns editable Orca project state.
- When logic could live in either C++ or a React page, it goes in the page unless there is a strong reason for C++: it touches Orca state, enforces a limit or boundary the app must guarantee, has to work without a page, or needs a thread or lifetime the page lacks. See [Where logic goes](architecture.md#where-logic-goes-the-page-first).
- Product policy lives in fork-owned files. OrcaSlicer-owned files receive only small, product-neutral, additive seams — every line changed there is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase.
- The user owns physical facts, object meaning, desired outcomes, privacy and legal decisions, and starting consequential physical actions.
- The production branch must not import experimental POC behavior merely because it demonstrated feasibility. Use the POC as evidence and reimplement through stable production boundaries.

## Source lineage

`jusprin-newui` and `jusprin-v2-poc` share base commit `8500fcdcca` (`v2.4.2`). The POC reference is pinned to final POC commit `9bba835b92`, so future changes to branch names do not make the historical evidence ambiguous.

9. [Local autosave and version history](autosave-version-history.md) — managed project storage, migration, restore, export, retention, and failure behavior.

Printer UI without hardware (Bambu in-process fake; control file; isolated app): [Fake Bambu README](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md). Print-host (Klipper/Moonraker) simulation stays on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter`.

## Governing decisions

- JusPrin is an AI-piloted 3D-printing product built on OrcaSlicer, not a replacement slicing engine.
- OrcaSlicer's C++ model, slicing pipeline, viewport, geometry operations, project serialization, and undo stack remain authoritative.
- The production application stays native C++/wxWidgets/OpenGL. The Agent conversation uses a local React/TypeScript application inside `wxWebView`.
- JavaScript renders state and submits typed commands; it never owns editable Orca project state.
- When logic could live in either C++ or a React page, it goes in the page unless there is a strong reason for C++: it touches Orca state, enforces a limit or boundary the app must guarantee, has to work without a page, or needs a thread or lifetime the page lacks. See [Where logic goes](architecture.md#where-logic-goes-the-page-first).
- Product policy lives in fork-owned files. OrcaSlicer-owned files receive only small, product-neutral, additive seams — every line changed there is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase.
- The user owns physical facts, object meaning, desired outcomes, privacy and legal decisions, and starting consequential physical actions.
- The production branch must not import experimental POC behavior merely because it demonstrated feasibility. Use the POC as evidence and reimplement through stable production boundaries.

## Source lineage

`jusprin-newui` and `jusprin-v2-poc` share base commit `8500fcdcca` (`v2.4.2`). The POC reference is pinned to final POC commit `9bba835b92`, so future changes to branch names do not make the historical evidence ambiguous.
